description.text:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development.
It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways,
without incrementing the interface major version and without prior
notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients
and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols
and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or
semantics remaining stable across releases.

This protocol provides two capabilities to privileged clients such as
display configuration panels:

1. Designating one connected output as the primary output, which the
compositor may use to decide placement of panels, notifications, and
newly opened windows.

2. Adjusting the color temperature and brightness of individual outputs
via a double-buffered pending/commit model.

Outputs in this protocol are addressed by opaque uuid strings instead
of wl_output objects. Clients obtain the uuid of an output from the
treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 protocol. A uuid remains stable
across sessions and output reconnections, which lets clients and the
compositor persist per-output settings and restore them after a
restart. In the primary_output event an empty uuid means that no
primary output is currently designated.

The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are
to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

A singleton global that exposes two capabilities: designating the
primary output and creating per-output picture control objects.

Only one client should bind this interface at a time. The compositor
may not advertise this global to additional clients, or may ignore
requests from them, while a binding is already active.

On binding, the compositor immediately emits a primary_output event
carrying the uuid of the currently designated primary output, or
an empty uuid if no primary output has been designated.
description.summary: primary output and picture control manager

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_output_manager_v2 object.

Existing treeland_output_picture_control_v2 objects created
through this manager are not affected and must be destroyed
separately by the client.

Designate the output identified by the given uuid as the
primary output. The compositor uses the primary output as a
hint for panel placement, initial window positioning, and
other compositor-defined policies.

The uuid must identify a currently connected, enabled output.
If the uuid is empty, or no enabled output with this uuid is
currently connected, the compositor rejects the request and
emits a primary_output_failed event with the invalid_output
reason; the primary output designation is unchanged. Neither
case is a protocol error, so a request carrying a stale uuid
never disconnects the client.

The compositor applies a successful change immediately and
confirms it by emitting a primary_output event carrying the
uuid of the newly designated primary output.
description.summary: designate an output as the primary output

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of an enabled output to designate as primary

description.text:
Create a treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object for the
output identified by the given uuid. The returned object
allows the client to adjust the color temperature and
brightness of that output.

The uuid must identify a currently connected, enabled output.
If the uuid is empty, or no enabled output with this uuid is
currently connected, the request still succeeds as long as the
new object id is valid: the picture control object is created,
but the compositor immediately emits a result event with the
invalid_output result, without waiting for a commit. Such a
uuid is not a protocol error. Once an invalid_output result
has been delivered on an object, the object is permanently
inert: only the destroy request is valid, and no further
result, color_temperature, or brightness events are emitted
on it. The object does not recover if an output with the same
uuid is connected later; the client must destroy the inert
object and call get_picture_control again to obtain a usable
one.

Multiple picture control objects may exist for the same output
at the same time; each object reports value changes
independently.
description.summary: create a picture control object for an output

args.name: id
args.summary: new picture control object for the given output

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of the output to control

description.text:
Emitted by the compositor to report the uuid of the current
primary output. This event is sent once immediately after the
client binds this interface, and again whenever the primary
output designation changes — whether in response to a
set_primary_output request or through a compositor-driven
fallback.

When the designated primary output is disconnected or disabled,
the compositor automatically selects another available output as
the new primary and emits this event with its uuid. When no
output is currently available, the event is emitted with an
empty uuid.

args.name: uuid
args.summary: uuid of the currently designated primary output, or empty when none is available

description.text:
Emitted when a set_primary_output request cannot be applied,
indicating that the primary output designation is unchanged.
The reason identifies why the request was rejected: no enabled
output with the provided uuid is currently connected.

args.name: reason
args.summary: why the set_primary_output request was rejected

description.text: Reasons returned by the primary_output_failed event.
description.summary: reasons a set_primary_output request was rejected

entries.name: invalid_output
entries.summary: the provided uuid is empty or no enabled output with this uuid is currently connected

description.text:
Represents a picture control session bound to the output
identified by its uuid, created by
treeland_output_manager_v2.get_picture_control.

Color temperature and brightness are managed via a double-buffered
pending/commit model. The client accumulates changes with
set_color_temperature and set_brightness, then atomically applies
them with a single commit request. After a successful commit the
compositor emits a color_temperature or brightness event for each
value that actually changed.

On creation with a uuid that identifies a live enabled output,
the compositor emits color_temperature and brightness events to
report the current values of the output before the client has
made any changes.

When the object is created for a uuid that does not identify a
live enabled output, the compositor immediately emits a result
event with the invalid_output result instead of the initial
color_temperature and brightness events.

An invalid_output result is terminal, whether it is delivered
immediately after creation or in response to a later commit: the
object becomes permanently inert, only the destroy request
remains valid, and no further events are emitted on it. The
object never recovers, even if an output with the same uuid is
connected afterwards; the client must destroy the inert object
and call get_picture_control again to obtain a new one.
description.summary: per-output color temperature and brightness control

description.text:
Destroy the treeland_output_picture_control_v2 object and
release all associated compositor resources. Any uncommitted
pending settings are discarded.

After this request the compositor will no longer send result,
color_temperature, or brightness events on this object.

Set the pending color temperature for the output. The value
is not applied until the client sends a commit request.

Valid range is [1000, 20000] Kelvin. A value outside this
range is rejected immediately with the
invalid_color_temperature protocol error, terminating the
connection; nothing is stored in the pending state and no
commit is required to clear the request.

Multiple calls before commit replace the pending value;
only the last value is applied.

args.name: temperature
args.summary: color temperature in Kelvin, in the range [1000, 20000]

description.text:
Set the pending brightness for the output. The value is not
applied until the client sends a commit request.

Valid range is [0.0, 100.0]. A value outside this range is
rejected immediately with the invalid_brightness protocol
error, terminating the connection; nothing is stored in the
pending state and no commit is required to clear the request.

Multiple calls before commit replace the pending value;
only the last value is applied.

Atomically apply all pending color temperature and brightness
values accumulated since the last commit. The compositor always
responds with a result event indicating success or failure.
After a successful commit the compositor emits a
color_temperature or brightness event for each value that
actually changed.

It is valid to call commit without any preceding set_* requests;
the compositor treats this as a no-op that succeeds without
changing any value.

A failed commit reports its cause through the result event.
Range validation of pending values is performed at set_*
time and never reaches a commit; a commit therefore only
fails because of the output: it does not support the requested
adjustment (unsupported, retrying the same settings is unlikely
to succeed), the uuid no longer identifies a live enabled
output (invalid_output), or the commit could not be applied
for a transient or unknown reason (failed). In every failure
case the applied settings remain unchanged.

An invalid_output result is terminal: it permanently
invalidates the object, so only destroy may be sent afterwards
and the object never recovers even if an output with the same
uuid is connected again.

Emitted by the compositor to report the outcome of a commit
request, and immediately after object creation when the object
was created for a uuid that does not identify a live enabled
output.

In response to a commit request the event is always sent,
including commits with no pending changes, to indicate whether
the settings were applied. Besides the failed, unsupported,
and invalid_output causes, no other result value is defined.
Out-of-range pending values are rejected at set_* time with a
fatal protocol error and never produce a commit result. After
a successful commit, a color_temperature or brightness event
is emitted for each value that actually changed.

An invalid_output result is terminal: once it is delivered,
the object is permanently inert, only the destroy request
remains valid, and no further events are emitted on it. The
object never recovers, even if an output with the same uuid
is connected afterwards; the client must destroy the object
and call get_picture_control again.
description.summary: result of a commit request or object creation

args.name: result
args.summary: whether the commit succeeded or failed, or the object was created for an invalid uuid

description.text:
Reports the currently applied color temperature of the output.
When the object is created for a live enabled output, this
event is emitted once immediately after creation to provide
the initial value. It is also emitted whenever the applied
color temperature changes — whether through a commit on this
object, a commit on another color control object for the same
output, or a compositor-driven change such as a system setting
update.

Color temperature is expressed in Kelvin on a Planckian locus,
in the range [1000, 20000].
description.summary: current color temperature of the output

description.text:
Reports the currently applied brightness of the output.
When the object is created for a live enabled output, this
event is emitted once immediately after creation to provide
the initial value. It is also emitted whenever the applied
brightness changes — whether through a commit on this object,
a commit on another picture control object for the same
output, or a compositor-driven change such as a system setting
update.

Brightness is expressed as a percentage in the range [0.0, 100.0].

args.name: brightness
args.summary: current brightness level in the range [0.0, 100.0]

description.text:
Raised by the compositor as a fatal protocol error when a
set_color_temperature or set_brightness request carries a
value outside its valid range. The connection is terminated
and no further requests are processed on this object.
description.summary: fatal protocol errors raised by set requests

entries.name: invalid_color_temperature
entries.summary: the color temperature is outside the valid range [1000, 20000]

entries.name: invalid_brightness
entries.summary: the brightness is outside the valid range [0.0, 100.0]

description.text:
Indicates the outcome of a commit request, or of object
creation when the object was created for a uuid that does not
identify a live enabled output. A commit is reported as
applied successfully, or as failed because the output does not
support the requested adjustment, because the associated
output is no longer available, or for another transient or
unknown reason. An invalid_output result is terminal: the
object becomes permanently inert and only destroy may be sent.
description.summary: result of a commit request or object creation

entries.name: success
entries.summary: all pending settings were applied successfully

entries.name: failed
entries.summary: the commit failed to apply for a transient or unknown reason; settings remain unchanged

entries.name: unsupported
entries.summary: the output does not support the requested adjustment, for example when its hardware cannot apply color temperature changes; settings remain unchanged

entries.name: invalid_output
entries.summary: the uuid does not identify a live enabled output; the object becomes permanently inert and settings remain unchanged
